He said the court had determined that replacing union conductors with managers constituted a “major dispute” and violated the railroad’s obligation to maintain existing working conditions. candidates.title: Genesee & Wyoming prepares to split into three rail holding companies
candidates.excerpt: Genesee & Wyoming Inc. is planning to separate into three rail holding companies, effective Jan. 1, 2027, a move that will position the regional entities for eventual sale. The companies will continue to be owned by G&W parent Brookfield and GIC. G&W operates more than 100 railroads. The new companies are: Atlantic & Great Lakes Transportation Inc., which will be made up of G&W operations in New England (including Berkshire & Eastern Railroad), New York, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. Atlantic & Great Lakes will be based in Rochester, N.Y., and led by Chief Executive Bill Keough, who has been with G&W for eight years and most recently served as regional senior vice president. Canyon & Cascade Transportation Inc., which will be comprised of G&W operations in Washington, Oregon, California, Arizona, and New Mexico. candidates.title: Intermodal leads U.S. rail traffic up 6.6% from a year ago
candidates.excerpt: Rail traffic among U.S. carriers rose 6.6% in the week ending Nov. 7 compared with the same week a year ago, driven by an 11% increase in intermodal shipments, the Association of American Railroads said. Carloads increased 1.3% from a year earlier. Seven of the 10 commodity groups recorded gains, led by motor vehicles and parts, up 10.4%, and forest products, up 10.1%. Metallic ores and metals followed with a 6.4% increase. Grain shipments declined 2.4%, nonmetallic minerals fell 1.7%, and coal slipped 1.2% among weaker volumes. Through the first 44 weeks of 2026, total U.S. rail traffic increased 3.9% compared with the same period in 2025. Intermodal volume rose 4.9%, carloads increased 2.7%. Grain remained the strongest-growing freight category year to date, up 9.7%, despite its weekly decline. Metallic ores and metals increased 8.8%, and petroleum and petroleum products rose 7.7%. candidates.title: Illinois Railway Museum acquires ex-Burlington bilevel gallery cars
candidates.excerpt: UNION, Ill. — The Illinois Railway Museum (IRM) has acquired a second complete and operational train of bilevel gallery cars, this one from the former Chicago, Burlington & Quincy Railroad. The stainless-steel consist of two coaches and a cab car arrived at the museum grounds on Wednesday night (Nov. 11), having spent approximately the last 20 years in Michigan. Coaches Nos. 702 and 709 were built by Budd in 1950 and were among the first gallery cars constructed. They were revolutionary, according to IRM. The Burlington’s new fleet offered air conditioning, sealed windows, and comfortable seats. The two-level design also permitted higher seating capacity, while the open gallery down the middle allowed conductors to collect fares from both levels simultaneously. In 1965, the Burlington followed the example of the Chicago & North Western’s push-pull operations by ordering its first bilevel cab cars. Cab car 791, built that year, was part of the initial order. candidates.excerpt: BREWSTER, Ohio — The Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen has ended its strike against the Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway. The union announced it ended the strike on the evening of Wednesday, Nov. 11, about nine hours after the walkout began at noon, after the railroad agreed not to allow company managers to serve as conductors. About 140 engineers and conductors launched the strike while claiming the use of managers as conductors violated the union’s contract, as well as a court order dating to 2013 regarding the issue at the W&LE. “We’re pleased that the railroad’s management has agreed to honor the contract, comply with the federal court order and return to the best safety practices,” BLET National President Mark Wallace said in a press release. “Conductors play a critical role in a two-person crew and train safety. candidates.title: GEODIS launches new rail freight connection between Italy and France
candidates.excerpt: GEODIS has launched a new rail freight service connecting Vicenza in northern Italy with Noisy-le-Sec, near Paris. The new route expands the company’s European intermodal network and provides another transport option for businesses in Italy’s Veneto region. The first train departed on 19 October 2026, marking the start of the service operated by Captrain and Hexafret. Both companies belong to Rail Logistics Europe, part of the SNCF Group alongside GEODIS. Initially, the service offers one departure per week in each direction. However, GEODIS plans to increase the frequency to two weekly departures per direction from January 2027. The connection is designed to transport several types of freight, including packaged liquid and powder goods. It also extends the company’s existing rail services in northern Italy, which already cover Lombardy, Piedmont and Emilia-Romagna through its Novara connection. candidates.title: New report identifies Hong Kong’s place in world shipping
candidates.excerpt: New report identifies Hong Kong’s place in world shipping Hong Kong Maritime Week is about to kick off. To celebrate the occasion, Splash today publishes a 48-page magazine on the city’s maritime hub credentials. A ship can be ordered at a mainland Chinese yard, owned through a leasing company in Hong Kong, insured in London, crewed through a management operation in Asia and chartered from Singapore. Its cargo need never pass through Hong Kong’s harbour. Even its Hong Kong financing vehicle may have to seek credit approval elsewhere. The geography of shipping has always been complicated. What has changed is the urgency with which Hong Kong must ask where the real business takes place. Is the city still a maritime capital in its own right, chosen by international owners, traders and financiers because of what it offers? AAR Reports Weekly Rail Traffic for the Week Ending October 31, 2026
candidates.excerpt: The Association of American Railroads (AAR) reported U.S. rail traffic for the week ending October 31, 2026. For this week, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 514,080 carloads and intermodal units, up 3.5 percent compared with the same week last year. Total carloads for the week ending October 31 were 233,816 carloads, up 3.0 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 280,264 containers and trailers, up 3.9 percent compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals, up 3,883 carloads, to 25,059; chemicals, up 2,542 carloads, to 34,523; and motor vehicles and parts, up 1,351 carloads, to 16,268. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were grain, down 2,092 carloads, to 23,078; miscellaneous carloads, down 1,162 carloads, to 8,369; and coal, down 224 carloads, to 55,042.
